Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old man with 3 days of frequent watery diarrhea following brief vomiting, no blood or abdominal pain; assessed as likely acute gastroenteritis. Supportive care advised (oral rehydration, paracetamol), time off work, and follow-up if not improved.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for ~3 days.
- Symptom details:
  - Frequency: ~5–6 loose, watery stools/day.
  - Onset: Began with nausea and 2 episodes of vomiting; vomiting has resolved.
  - Associated symptoms: Feels weak; feels dehydrated; poor appetite; minimal solid intake.
  - Denies: Visible blood in stool, abdominal pain, headaches, muscle pains.
  - Fever/temperature: Felt somewhat warm at onset; currently feels fine.
- Triggers/exposures:
  - No recalled suspicious food/takeaway.
  - No known sick contacts.
  - Onset occurred at home while working at a computer.
- Course: Persistent over 3 days; vomiting resolved; diarrhea ongoing.
- Function: Missed work for the past 3 days.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma; uses a “blue” reliever inhaler infrequently (exacerbation triggers not detailed).

Medications:
- Asthma “blue” inhaler (name/dose/route/frequency not documented), used infrequently.
- Paracetamol recommended for fever/weakness (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) recommended (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Occupation: Software engineer.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks infrequently/socially.
- Recently off work for 3 days due to illness; advised to remain off until diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours.

Family History:
- Father: Hypertension; died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago.
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None ordered/documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute watery diarrhea, likely viral gastroenteritis.
  - Plan:
    - Oral hydration; encourage increased fluid intake.
    - Oral rehydration salts (Dioralyte).
    - Paracetamol as needed for feverishness/weakness.
    - Rest; continue time off work for 1–2 days.
    - Return to work after being diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours.
    - Follow-up: If not improved by next week, return for reassessment.
- Issue 2: Symptoms suggestive of dehydration (subjective thirst/weakness, reduced oral intake).
  - Plan:
    - Emphasize frequent small sips of fluids and use of oral rehydration solution.
    - Gradual reintroduction of light foods as tolerated.
- Issue 3: Asthma (stable).
  - Plan:
    - Continue reliever inhaler as needed (no changes documented).

General Plan items:
- Safety net: Advised to return next week if not improving; no additional red-flag instructions documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; hydration status exam; abdominal exam; stool volume/odor; recent travel; recent antibiotic use; recent hospitalization; occupational exposures; COVID/respiratory review; medication list reconciliation (only inhaler documented); detailed dosing for recommended OTCs.
- Internal conflicts: None noted (patient initially felt warm/possible low-grade fever, now resolved).
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor fillers and brief interruptions, but clinical content understandable.
